experiments.description: RMCA-Hybrid will improve EM accuracy by combining delta rule updates with gating mechanisms for more stable memory writing.

hypothesis.hypothesis: RMCA-Hybrid will improve EM accuracy by combining delta rule updates with gating mechanisms for more stable memory writing.
hypothesis.rationale: Implementing human_directions item #19 (RMCA-Hybrid). This is a pending suggestion from the priority list that must be addressed before hyperparameter tuning. The hybrid architecture combines delta rule memory updates with gating for better gradient flow and memory stability during associative retrieval.
hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__, add two new parameters: self.use_delta_rule (default True) and self.use_gating (default True). In the forward method, modify the memory write operation to use a hybrid update: compute write_residual via memory_write attention, then apply gating: memory = memory + gate * write_residual where gate = sigmoid(gate_proj(write_residual)). Add a new learnable gate_proj linear layer initialized to zeros. Also add a delta parameter alpha for the update: memory = memory + alpha * gated_write_residual. Add config options num_mem_heads to RMCAConfig if not present.

experiments.description: RMCA-Hybrid will improve EM accuracy by implementing a gated delta rule for memory updates, allowing the model to learn how much new information to incorporate into memory versus retaining existing states.

hypothesis.hypothesis: RMCA-Hybrid will improve EM accuracy by implementing a gated delta rule for memory updates, allowing the model to learn how much new information to incorporate into memory versus retaining existing states.
hypothesis.rationale: Implementing human direction item #19 (RMCA-Hybrid) takes absolute priority over hyperparameter tuning. This combines delta rule memory updates with gating mechanisms to enable more stable and selective memory writing, which should improve associative retrieval accuracy on the KV task.
hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer class __init__ method, add a new parameter self.memory_write_gate = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1, num_mem_tokens, 1)) after self.memory_state_norm initialization. In the forward method, modify the memory write update section to apply gating: after computing write_residual from memory_write, multiply it by torch.sigmoid(self.memory_write_gate) before adding to memory. Ensure the gate parameter is properly initialized and included in the layer's parameters.

experiments.description: RMCA-Delta will improve EM accuracy by implementing a learnable delta update mechanism for memory states instead of simple additive residual connections.

hypothesis.hypothesis: RMCA-Delta will improve EM accuracy by implementing a learnable delta update mechanism for memory states instead of simple additive residual connections.
hypothesis.rationale: Human directions #19 (RMCA-Hybrid) was already tried in iterations 1-2 and reverted. Following the 'Do not repeat a change that has already been tried' rule, I implement the next untried pending item #17 (RMCA-Delta). No hyperparameters have been exhausted yet per the HYPERPARAMETER-FIRST POLICY, but human_directions take absolute priority per the CRITICAL RULES.
hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__, add: (1) a learnable scalar gate parameter self.delta_gate initialized to 0.0, (2) a learnable scaling parameter self.delta_scale initialized to 1.0. In MemoryAugmentedLayer.forward, modify the memory update line 'memory = memory + write_residual' to 'memory = memory + self.delta_scale * self.delta_gate * write_residual'. Register both parameters as nn.Parameter with requires_grad=True.

hypothesis.instruction: Add a gated delta update mechanism to MemoryAugmentedLayer.forward(): (1) After computing write_residual, create a learnable gate parameter (sigmoid) that scales the update, (2) Replace the simple addition 'memory = memory + write_residual' with 'memory = memory + gate * write_residual', (3) Initialize gate to 0.5 to start with partial updates, (4) Ensure gate is per-layer and trainable via nn.Parameter with appropriate initialization.
